items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Rose Tizol came with us on the tour, and she was worried about me, because she was a dear person

ctx.x: So you had a really good rapport with the band – the guys in the band.

It was beautiful. Every guy in that band was beautiful. It’s a family. It was a family band. We shared everything. Even on that tour. You were asking about that tour, Big Show of 1951? The three main characters were Duke Ellington’s band, Sarah Vaughan, and Nat “King” Cole. That was really segregated. We played all those places down South. Birmingham, Alabama, was the first one. They still had all the signs up. “Colored only.” “White only.” So I would hang out with the band. I’d be eating next to Nat “King” Cole…

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: I knew both of them; Pearl and I were friends.

ctx.x: Oh, I thought it was you?
No, I was home. I knew both of them; Pearl and I were friends.

No, we was at the Howard Theatre, and Pearl was getting ready to start working in a white club there, and she happened to be across the street from the stage -- that's where everybody eat, and so forth, and Louie was coming out, and I said, "Louie, come here, I want for you to meet Pearl Bailey." "Pearl Bailey?" He said, "Well, naturally." He said I'm opening tonight at the club so and so, and I wish you'd bring Louie with you tonight after you get through." I said, "Sure" and we went over there, and Pearl opened…
